title: Kuching Marathon Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
seo_title: Kuching Marathon Review: The 2025 Edition | Sarawak
meta_description: Kuching Marathon review: the 2025 edition drew a record 14,150 runners and a Kenyan sweep. The 2026 race was cancelled for haze the day before.
dek: The 2026 Kuching Marathon was called off at the last minute because of haze. The last edition that was actually run, in September 2025, drew a record field. Here is what it was like.
verdict: The Kuching Marathon is one of the biggest road races in Borneo: its tenth edition, on 21 September 2025, drew a record 14,150 participants across four distances from Padang Merdeka [1]. Kenyan runners swept the open marathon and half marathon, while Malaysians won the national titles [1]. The 2026 edition, due on 27 September, never happened. It was cancelled at the last minute because of the haze over Kuching, with more than 13,000 runners registered and many of them already booked into hotels and flights [2]. If you are planning around the next edition, the lesson of 2026 is that a late-September date in Sarawak carries a real haze risk.

sections.heading: The 2026 Race That Did Not Happen
paragraphs: The organisers cancelled the Kuching Marathon 2026, scheduled for Sunday 27 September, because of the haze affecting Kuching and the surrounding areas [2]. The call came at the eleventh hour: more than 13,000 runners had registered, many from outside Sarawak, and some had already paid for flights, hotels and homestays [2].

Sarawak's Minister for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development, Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, said he had visited the race pack collection venue without being told of the cancellation, and that he believed the organisers had valid reasons, possibly on the advice of the police and the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee [2]. He also acknowledged the criticism on social media from runners who had spent money to be there [2].

Police had already announced 26 road closures and diversions around Kuching for race weekend, from noon on 26 September to 10am on 27 September [3]. Nothing in the reporting suggests the race was badly organised. It was stopped by air quality, which no organiser controls.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition in Numbers
paragraphs: The last Kuching Marathon to be run was the tenth edition, on Sunday 21 September 2025. It drew a record 14,150 participants across four categories: 42 km, 21 km, 10 km and 5 km [1]. Prizes were presented at Padang Merdeka by the mayor of the Kuching North City Commission (DBKU) [1].
The field was on the same scale again in 2026, when more than 13,000 had signed up before the cancellation [2]. This is a big race, and race-week logistics should be planned with that in mind.

sections.heading: A Kenyan Sweep at the Front
paragraphs: Kenyan runners took both open long-distance races. David Rono won the men's marathon in 2:26:21, leading a Kenyan clean sweep ahead of Hosea Kogei and David Kipsang, and Abigael Jerop won the women's marathon in 3:15:19 [1]. In the half marathon, Job Minacho Kamonde won the men's open title in 1:09:31 [1].

Not everything went to Kenya. Malaysia's Jia Xin Cheng won the women's open half marathon in 1:41:58, Brunei's Ruzaini Mahadi won the men's open 10 km in 37:11, and Lee Siok Chin won the women's veteran marathon in 3:18:41, which also made her the top Malaysian woman [1]. Hazarullah Safri was the top Malaysian man, in 2:46:04 [1].
For most runners, the useful point is that this is a tropical race run in September. Treat it as a hot-weather marathon and pace it that way rather than chasing a time set somewhere cooler.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Every distance starts and finishes at Padang Merdeka, in the old centre of Kuching [1][3]. For 2026 the police closed or diverted roads from 12.01am on race morning until 10am, including routes towards Padang Merdeka and several of the city's main roundabouts [3]. That gives a rough idea of the course window: runners are expected to be off the roads by mid-morning.

Race pack collection is in the days before the race. In 2026 it had already opened when the cancellation was announced [2]. If you fly in, plan to arrive at least a day early. In a haze season, also make sure your flights and room can be changed.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next One?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a large, well-supported city race in Borneo. The 2025 field was a record, the front of the race attracts international athletes, and there are four distances to choose from.

The caveat is the date. A race in late September in Sarawak can be caught by regional haze, and 2026 shows what that costs a travelling runner. Book refundable travel, and watch the organiser's channels and the air quality forecast in the final week.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition and on the cancellation of the 2026 race. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: Why was the Kuching Marathon 2026 cancelled?
faqs.answer: Because of the haze affecting Kuching and the surrounding areas. The organisers called the race off at the last minute, before its Sunday 27 September 2026 date, with more than 13,000 runners registered. Sarawak's sports minister said he believed the decision may have followed advice from the police and the state disaster management committee.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Kuching Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: A record 14,150 participants took part in the tenth edition on Sunday 21 September 2025, across the 42 km, 21 km, 10 km and 5 km categories from Padang Merdeka. The 2026 race had more than 13,000 registered before it was cancelled for haze, so the field is consistently in five figures.

faqs.question: Who won the Kuching Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: Kenya's David Rono won the men's marathon in 2:26:21 and Abigael Jerop the women's in 3:15:19. Job Minacho Kamonde won the men's open half marathon in 1:09:31, and Malaysia's Jia Xin Cheng the women's in 1:41:58. Hazarullah Safri and Lee Siok Chin were the top Malaysian marathoners.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the last edition that was actually run (21 September 2025), after the 2026 race was cancelled for haze. Replaces a pre-race preview. No rating: the sources are news reports, which describe how the event was run, not how runners rated it.
